clue.text: Engineer Queen engaged to get clever solution to rain problem

indicators.note: engaged in the sense of locked inside, so the royal letters sit within the engineer's name

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard Queen abbreviation
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A royal and an engineer join forces to come up with a smart fix for a downpour difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: A water table in building is a projecting ledge or moulding that throws rainwater clear of the wall below, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this term names a sloping ledge built to shed rainwater away from a wall.

clue.text: Egyptian perhaps saying prayers quietly in bed

indicators.note: in places the soft letter inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone from Egypt murmurs their prayers softly while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Coptic Church is an Egyptian Christian, so one who prays; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Colleague is disagreeable woman, pig oozing power

parts.note: cow is slang for an unpleasant woman

indicators.note: oozing suggests something leaking out, so that letter leaves the word for the pig

parts.note: a porker is a pig fattened for meat

explanation.surface: An unflattering office complaint about a fellow worker who is losing her grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow employee working alongside you is a colleague.

clue.text: Was forced to wear my long garment

indicators.note: wearing puts something around oneself, so the exclamation goes round the verb

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
'had to' means was forced to, so had stands for was forced

explanation.surface: Someone complains of having been made to put on a lengthy item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive here but a British exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chador is a long cloak covering head and body, worn by some Muslim women, especially in Iran.

clue.text: Chemical extracted from hole finally

indicators.note: extracted from tells us the letters are drawn out of a run of the clue words

explanation.surface: Some substance is drawn out of a hole at last.
explanation.definitionFit: An olefin is an alkene, an unsaturated hydrocarbon compound.

clue.text: First hint of annoyance in diner — one letting off a rocket?

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for the diner

parts.note: a luncher is someone eating a meal, a diner

indicators.note: first hint of picks out only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A diner becomes irritated and then tells someone off sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting off a rocket' reads as giving someone a telling-off, a British idiom, but the definition is literal: someone who fires a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A launcher is a person or device that sends a rocket into flight.

clue.text: No longer having means of transport, a woman left out of the marriage

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
a tram is a vehicle for carrying passengers
Rita, a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman without a car steps outside her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramarital describes something such as an affair happening outside a marriage.

clue.text: A rower bathed after wrecking device to keep water out

indicators.note: wrecking a set of words leaves them to be rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A rower takes a bath after wrecking his boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A weatherboard is a sloping board fixed to the foot of a door or a wall to shed rain.

clue.text: Autumn accommodation to prove ineffective

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a flat is an apartment, a place to live

explanation.surface: Renting a place in autumn turns out to be a poor move.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for failing to have the intended effect, as a joke that gets no laugh.

clue.text: Novel devoured by guy is hit

indicators.note: something devoured is taken inside, so the novel goes within the teasing word

parts.note: to cod or to guy someone is to tease or make fun of them
She is H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel

explanation.surface: A book is eaten up by some man, who is then struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new' and 'guy' like a man; here they are Haggard's novel SHE and the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Coshed means struck with a cosh, a heavy club or truncheon.

clue.text: Position no longer in abeyance, we'd conjecture?

definitions.meaning: a post or job, such as a public appointment

definitions.text: no longer in abeyance, we'd conjecture?
definitions.meaning: a matter in abeyance is 'on ice', so one taken back out of storage is jokingly no longer on it, the opposite preposition

explanation.surface: A post that is no longer suspended, or so we might guess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We'd conjecture?' flags a whimsical coinage: the opposite of 'on ice', meaning postponed, read as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a post or position of authority, such as a public office.

clue.text: Appeal of little French home full of love

parts.note: petit is French for little

indicators.note: full of means the home word has the love letter inside it

parts.note: in means at home
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A request made by a small French household brimming with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A petition is a formal request or appeal to an authority.

clue.text: Head of Latin in school is stylish

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for a school

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The head of Latin at the school dresses fashionably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a classroom, but here it is a group of whales, a GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Glam, short for glamorous, means showily stylish.

clue.text: The red Etna, getting wilder, looked ominous

indicators.note: getting wilder suggests the letters running riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The fiery volcano in Sicily grew more violent and looked menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that threatened gave signs of impending danger, so looked menacing.

clue.text: Short request couched in a rotten fit of anger

indicators.note: couched in means lying inside, so the shortened request goes within the outer words

parts.note: poxy is slang for rotten or worthless

indicators.note: short tells us the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a plea is a request

explanation.surface: A brief appeal is made inside a lousy outburst of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couched' suggests lying on a sofa, but here it just means set inside; POXY is British slang for shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy is used figuratively for extreme rage, as in apoplectic with fury.

clue.text: I may manifest energy in two ways

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
go also means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: Someone claims to show vigour in more than one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two ways' tells you to express energy twice, once as E and once as GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' of psychology.

clue.text: Sign shows where Canterbury pilgrims will go shortly?

indicators.note: shortly says the phrase is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Canterbury is in the county of Kent, so its pilgrims go 'to Kent'

explanation.surface: A signpost points the way for pilgrims heading to the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England containing Canterbury; TO KENT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or symbol, as in a token of affection.

clue.text: Criminal den from which one emerges after food's been served up

indicators.note: after places the trimmed den behind the turned food word
in a down clue, served up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: from which points back to the den as the word the letter leaves
one emerging from the den means that letter comes out of the word for a den

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A thief's hideout, which someone leaves once the meal has been dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB written upwards gives BURG; LAIR loses its I to give LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: Face death almost — feature of board game

indicators.note: almost removes the final letter of the word for death

parts.note: end can mean death
a counter is a playing piece in a board game

explanation.surface: A player nearly loses everything while moving pieces about a board.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter something is to meet or confront it, to face it.

clue.text: Ministers in one part of the church look ridiculous, vacant

parts.note: the chancel is the area near the altar of a church
lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Clergy standing in the chancel look absurd and blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' tempts towards clergy, but these are government ministers, such as the British finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancellors are senior government ministers, as with the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer.

clue.text: Demonstrated in favour of archdeacon

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Ven, for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Support for a senior churchman is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Proven means shown to be true, demonstrated.

clue.text: Favouring woven fabric, this writer's seen in Scottish town

parts.note: for means in favour of
twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs
this writer's means 'I am', the setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: An author who likes a particular cloth turns up in a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort William is a town in the Scottish Highlands beneath Ben Nevis.

clue.text: Most miserable, forcing a set smile

indicators.note: forcing a set of letters means bending them into a new shape

explanation.surface: The unhappiest person is the one putting on a fixed grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Measliest means meanest or most paltry, the superlative of measly.

clue.text: Reportedly developed very much like a monster

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the phrase is matched to a word of the same sound

parts.note: grew means developed and some can mean very much, giving the phrase said

explanation.surface: It is said that something grew enormously, like a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrifying and repellent, as a monster would be.

clue.text: Fiery person badly hurt, so must keep quiet

indicators.note: keeping something is holding it inside, so the jumble goes round the soft letter
badly signals the preceding words are to be jumbled

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone in pain is told to keep the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the two words to HOTSUR before the quiet letter goes in; 'Fiery' is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotspur, the nickname of Sir Henry Percy, means a rash, hot-headed person.

clue.text: Allowed to be bad after end of school

indicators.note: after puts the word for bad behind that last letter
end of picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: awful means very bad

explanation.surface: Being naughty is permitted once school is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful means permitted by law, allowed.

clue.text: Cathedral's original extravagant article that a cleric might wear

indicators.note: original means the beginning, so the first letter of the word

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ornate item from the cathedral's early days that a priest might put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Maybe oak's not right for one type of support

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is removed

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Perhaps an oak is not the right choice for holding something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The support is the golf peg on which a ball sits for driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is the small peg supporting a golf ball before it is struck.
